name: Ava Boyd
life: “I still remember the mural disappearing beneath a trial patch of white.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Ava takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I was going to clean the paint off for free. I offered the city my labor for a new panel instead.
appearance: Ava has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for a center part and straight chestnut hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a mustard canvas overshirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Ava starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Ava is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Ava loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To provide a fresh panel without wiping out the old one.
family: Ethan Wells is Ava’s stepsibling. Ava remembers the birthdays. Ethan asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *An old restaurant debt*, Ethan says, “I arrived expecting interest. The owner wants the name of the singer from the service.”
connections: Jody Gao. They propose a new panel beside the original painted scar.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Ava helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.
